extracted.intended_audience: professional and freelance photojournalists, multimedia journalists, picture editors, and publications submitting to the 71st Pictures of the Year International competition
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and judging rules for the 71st Pictures of the Year International (POYi) competition covering eligibility, category descriptions, technical file specifications, digital-processing standards, entry limits, fees, and judging criteria for stills, multimedia, and editing entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Processing and "App" Filters
rubrics_metrics.description: POYi accepts two photographic modes: color and black & white. For color images, the goal is to replicate what the human eye experiences. Routine image correction for color toning, white balance, and exposure is acceptable. Black & white images should display a full grayscale range from deep-shadow blacks to highlight whites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photos from mobile-device cameras are eligible, but the use of software capture filters (Hipstamatic, CameraBag, Instragram) that artificially impose on the integrity of the scene with excessive tonal aberrations, textures, vignetting, or other artistic abstractions may be disqualified. Judges will disqualify entries they feel over-manipulate the image. Prohibited: digital manipulation or alteration of content, manufactured photo illustrations, double exposures, added masks, borders, backgrounds, text, handwritten notes, or other artistic effects. Diptychs and triptychs are not eligible. Film edges are allowed only if they are the true nature of the medium (negative/ transparency/Polaroid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture Stories — Eligibility, Structure, and Entry Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: "Freelance/Agency" photo story and portfolio categories are open to all photographers. "Newspaper" photo story and portfolio categories are only open to photographers employed as staff members for a regularly published newspaper (part-time/stringers with exclusive/majority agreements may enter). A photographer’s stories must be entered consistently in the same division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries "must have been taken or published for the first time during 2013." A few pre-2013 images are acceptable if integral to a story and unpublished. Entries should have a clearly defined structure with each image contributing something different; literal chronological stories and thematic essays are both acceptable but logical organization is essential. Edit tightly and eliminate weak/redundant images. A picture story may be entered only once; do not re-edit the same photos and submit as a different version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia Stories — Documentary Approach and Judging Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to everyone — teams or individuals, independent or affiliated. Stories should conform to a documentary approach with journalistic standards and appraise storytelling in still and/or motion photojournalism with audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observational and direct cinema techniques; goal is to "show" the story rather than have an interviewee "tell" it. Judging criteria: news value, visual aesthetics, audio quality, overall narrative structure. Ineligible: staged reenactments, business/organization promotions, personal portfolios, stories where the funding organization is the primary subject. Multimedia stories must be shot or published online during 2013, cannot have been entered in the prior year's competition, and should be submitted as a single primary active URL; do not upload original .mov/.mp4/.m4v/.swf files; links must be active through judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo Editing — Selection, Organization, and Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo editing should demonstrate sensitivity for the selection and organization of documentary photography. Page design should reflect consideration for the reader and respect for the vision of the photographer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All stories must be published in 2013. Judges consider effectiveness of captions, headlines, and other display typography as well as photo content. Aggressive local coverage and imaginative editing of wire and syndicated photos are important. Design and presentation of inside pages and section fronts will be evaluated. Entries should be tightened to remove weak display or type-heavy pages. Submit each page as a separate PDF; a doubletruck/spread should be submitted as a single PDF. A published story may be submitted only once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spirit of the Competition — Documentary Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Show truth with a camera" is the guiding principle. Images should reflect news events and social issues with respect for the integrity of the scene and the intent of the moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scenes that are set up or staged by the photographer do not honor documentary photography (portrait categories are the exception). Color toning/exposure corrections should replicate what the human eye experiences. Content should not be digitally manipulated or altered. Story summaries and caption information should meet journalistic standards for accuracy and be ready-for-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Guidelines — Authorship, Authenticity, and Captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Still photography entries must be the work of only one person with a single credit line. All photographs must be true representations of the scene and cannot be posed, set up, or staged (portraits excepted). Photographs entered must have been taken or published for the first time between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each photograph must have a caption, and each picture story must include a summary that meets journalistic standards for accuracy and ready-for-publication. A photograph’s content and subjects must not be digitally manipulated or altered. Color toning and exposure correction should be routine adjustments that attempt to replicate what the human eye experiences. See "Digital Processing" rules for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singles & Photo Stories — File and Entry Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: One image per .JPG file. No diptychs. A single photograph may be submitted only once among the single-picture categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single photograph may appear as part of a picture story but in no more than one story. A picture story may be entered only once. A picture story consists of 3 to 12 photos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freelance & Newspaper Divisions Definition and Consistent Entry
rubrics_metrics.description: "Freelance/Agency" categories are open to all photographers; "Newspaper" categories are only open to photographers employed as staff of a regularly published newspaper. Part-time/stringers may enter Newspaper if their freelance agreement is exclusive to one newspaper or is the majority of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A photographer’s stories and portfolio must be entered consistently in the same division — either Newspaper or Freelance/Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Specifications — Stills, Editing Pages, and Multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Still photography files: .JPG, image size 3,000 pixels or larger on the longer side, resolution 300 dpi minimum. Editing page files: PDF, Quality: "High Quality Print."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit each page as a separate PDF file; do not group pages or embed files together. A doubletruck/spread should be submitted as a single PDF file. Multimedia entries: provide a single primary active URL link; links must be active through judging dates. Secured or password-protected Vimeo links are not accepted. Do not attempt to upload original .mov, .mp4, .m4v, or .swf files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration & Entry Process
rubrics_metrics.description: POYi uses an online registration and uploading process: create an account/login, fill in registration info, build your entry by selecting categories and uploading files, review entry, then submit and go to checkout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each registration (photographer or editing team) requires payment of $50 (U.S. dollars). Confirmation receipts will be emailed. The online system allows re-login to add, replace, or rearrange photos before submission. Deadline enforced (Jan. 16, 2014 at 11:59 p.m. CST).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation Logins and Submission Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each photographer whose work is entered must create an individual registration login.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers may enter a maximum of 15 submissions in any combination of categories. Organizations may enter work on behalf of photojournalists, but must create an individual registration for each photographer entered. Avoid duplicate entries between agency and photographer. Editing and multimedia organizations may create a single "team" registration and enter multiple editors’ work up to 15 submissions. Entries will not be reclassified or moved by judges; they may be moved before judging begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a "Submission" (counts toward 15 limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single "submission" may be: one photo in a single-picture category; one picture story (3–12 photographs); one project (40 photographs) in certain Premier award categories; an entry in a multimedia category; an entry in an editing category; a Photographer of the Year portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific counts and category inclusions determine how many of the allowed 15 submissions are used; refer to category definitions for exact limits (e.g., project = 40 photographs).

rubrics_metrics.name: $50 Payment and Extra Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Online payments accept Visa, MasterCard, and Discover. Organizations may sponsor multiple entrants with combined payment. $50 (U.S. dollars) per registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an extra $50 for certain entries: entries in the "Best Publications" division (#32-36), Multimedia Photographer of the Year, Documentary Project of the Year (covers three submitted projects), and some Premier categories. Exception: if entering only a single Best Photography Book or Best eBook and no other categories, a single $50 is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winner Notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners will be posted on a specified date and all winners will be contacted immediately after results are announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the 71st POYi winners will be posted Wednesday, Feb. 26, 2014.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 1 - Science & Natural History (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs that increase understanding and appreciation of science or the natural world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate accuracy, clarity, and ability to increase understanding/appreciation of science and natural subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 2 - Science & Natural History Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-picture story, essay, sequence, or series that increases understanding and appreciation for science or the natural world. Twelve photographs maximum per entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess storytelling clarity, selection of images to communicate scientific/natural history content, and adherence to the 12-photo maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 3 - General News (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs from a news event or social issue for which planning was possible — distinct from breaking spot news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge newsworthiness, composition, relevance to a planned news event or social issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 4 - Natural Disaster (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs from a natural disaster such as major storms, floods, or other acts of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ability to document natural disasters with impact, context, and ethical consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5 - Spot News (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs of breaking news or unplanned events taken during daily coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess immediacy, impact, and visual documentation of unplanned breaking events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 6 - Feature (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs, candid and unposed, that reflect the human experience, celebrate life, or chronicle a cultural trend. Respect for the dignity of the subject is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge emotional resonance, candidness, and dignity of subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 7 - Portrait (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs of a person that reveal the essence of the subject's character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ability to reveal character, composition, and portrait-making skill. Portrait categories are an exception to the non-staged rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 8 - Portrait Series
rubrics_metrics.description: A themed series of portraits that reveals the essence of the subjects' character. Seven photographs maximum per series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess thematic coherence across portraits and ability to reveal character; seven-photo max.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories 9–10 - News Picture Story (Newspaper and Freelance/Agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiple-picture story, essay, sequence, or series based on daily coverage of general news or breaking news. Twelve photographs maximum per story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories cannot be entered in more than one multiple-picture story category; evaluate narrative clarity, editing, and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories 11–12 - Issue Reporting Picture Story (Newspaper and Freelance/Agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiple-picture story that explores an important social, economic, or political issue. Twelve photographs maximum per story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge depth of issue exploration, storytelling, and image selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories 13–14 - Feature Picture Story (Newspaper and Freelance/Agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiple-picture story that reflects the human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend. Respect for the dignity of the subject is important. Twelve photographs maximum per story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate narrative, thematic treatment, and respect for subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 15 - Sports Action (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs that capture the peak action of individual or team sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timing, technical execution, and ability to capture peak action. Jubilation/dejection/reaction shots belong in Sports Feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 16 - Sports Feature (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs that increase understanding and appreciation for individual and team sports and spotlight emotion, celebration, jubilation, dejection, and reaction among athletes and fans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge emotional storytelling and context rather than peak action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 17 - Recreational Sports (Single)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs that celebrate the role of community leagues, amateur enthusiasts, intramural contests in sports, encouraging attention to smaller events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess celebration of community sports and attention to underreported athletic contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 18 - Sports Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiple-picture story that increases understanding and appreciation for individual and team sports and/or the role athletics play in lives of athletes and fans. Twelve photographs maximum per story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge diversity of images, narrative, and representation of sports' role in life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 19 - News Multimedia Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A multimedia story or essay based on coverage of general news or breaking news. Each entry should be a single news story or essay under six minutes in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess newsworthiness, multimedia integration, storytelling under six minutes; longer pieces should go to Documentary Journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 20 - Issue Reporting Multimedia Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A multimedia story that explores an important social, economic, or political issue; single story or essay under six minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate depth of issue exploration, multimedia execution, and narrative clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 21 - Feature Multimedia Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A multimedia story that reflects the human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend. Respect for dignity is important. Each entry should be under six minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge feature storytelling, audio/visual aesthetics, and respect for subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 22 - Sports Multimedia Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A multimedia story that increases understanding and appreciation for sports and/or the role athletics play in lives of athletes and fans. Each entry should be under six minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess storytelling, multimedia craft, and attention to sports' role; longer entries go to Documentary Journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 23 - Documentary Journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: A multimedia story that adopts concepts of documentary film using observational and direct cinema techniques with extended length up to 35 minutes. Stories should conform to documentary approach with journalistic standards focusing on news events, social issues, or cultural trends of 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary here is defined as storytelling grounded in truth relying on visual evidence with real subjects presenting themselves as themselves. Excludes fictional allegories, historical reenactments, docu-dramas, or TV news reports where on-camera commentator tells the story. Shorter edited versions cannot be entered in categories 19–22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories 24–25 - News & Issue Story Editing (Newspaper and Magazine)
rubrics_metrics.description: A published news story or essay based on daily coverage of general news, breaking news, or an issue-related story that explores an important social, economic, or political issue. Entries must be from a single issue, of one or more pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges evaluate selection, sequencing, typography, and presentation within a single issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories 26–27 - Feature Story Editing (Newspaper and Magazine)
rubrics_metrics.description: A published feature story or essay that reflects the human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend. Must be from a single issue, one or more pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess feature presentation and editing choices that support human-interest storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 28 - Sports Story Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: A sports story or essay published in a magazine or newspaper based on event coverage or features. Entries must be from a single issue, one or more pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category combines Newspaper and Magazine entries; judges evaluate editing choices specific to sports coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 29 - Series or Special Section
rubrics_metrics.description: One topic covered in one or more issues of a magazine or newspaper, or in a reprinted edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess thematic coherence across issues and editorial presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories 30–31 - Picture Editing Portfolios (Newspaper and Magazine)
rubrics_metrics.description: A picture editing portfolio may be submitted by an individual editor, a team, or both. A portfolio entry should present less than 40 pages. A magazine spread or newspaper doubletruck is considered one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit tightly; judges evaluate overall editing strategy, sequencing, selection, and page design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 32 - Best eBook
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes a story, series, or an extensive, long-term documentary photography project presented on an ePublishing platform. Content not limited to 2013; may be photographed anytime within the last three years (2011–2013). Photographs may be the work of one or more photographers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts apps, downloadable PDFs, mobile-optimized websites, or other digital publishing forms. Provide directions for download and any required credentials (iTunes/Amazon logins) on registration form. Extra $50 applies unless this is the only entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 33 - Best Website
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to online sites affiliated with news organizations, newspapers, magazines, or specialty advocacy organizations; recognizes overall excellence in use of photojournalism, interactive design, and multimedia storytelling on websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one entry per organization. Judges will review site home page, photo gallery/multimedia page, and three specific multimedia stories (provide URLs for each). Portfolios, business promotions, catalogs, or personal websites are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 34 - Best Newspaper
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one entry per publication. Submit the three best issues from any dates during 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging based on overall excellence across three issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 35 - Best Magazine
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one entry per publication. Submit the three best issues from any dates during 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate magazine-wide photojournalism and editorial quality across issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 36 - Best Photography Book (Premier Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: Book entries must rely on documentary photography and have been published sometime within the last three years (2011–2013). Photographs may be by one or more photographers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographer and publishing house should coordinate to avoid duplicate entries. Previous entries not eligible. Mail one print-bound copy with a "Best" label on the inside back cover. Extra $50 per entry (unless only a single book entry with no other categories). Trophy and cash prize honor photographer(s), publisher recognized with a plaque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 37 - Photographer of the Year - Newspaper (Premier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Premier category only open to photographers employed as staff members for a regularly published newspaper. Submit a maximum of 50 photographs as a portfolio including singles and at least two multiple-picture stories; stories are not limited to 12 images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singles should not be repeated in picture stories. Arrange singles and stories in the order for review (judges view singles first, then stories). No need for blank black JPG separation (program adds title slides). Photographers should enter single and picture story categories so judges know the work before portfolios are judged. POYi will not separate a portfolio into individual categories; upload separate files if entering individual categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 38 - Photographer of the Year - Freelance/Agency (Premier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to independent, freelance, self-employed, agency, or wire service photographers. Submit up to 50 photographs, with a diverse portfolio including singles and at least two multiple-picture stories (stories not limited to 12 images).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same portfolio rules as Category 37 regarding ordering, duplicates, and separate uploads for individual category entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 39 - Sports Photographer of the Year (Premier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to everyone. Submit a maximum of 30 photographs; portfolio should be diverse with single pictures and at least one multiple-picture story (stories not limited to 12 images).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All photographs must be taken during 2013. Represent at least three different sports. Singles should not repeat within picture stories. Arrange portfolio order for judging; judges view singles first. POYi will not separate portfolio images into individual categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 40 - Multimedia Photographer of the Year (Premier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to everyone. Stories must have been shot, produced, or published during 2013. The multimedia portfolio must be the work of one individual photojournalist or videographer who shot the principal visual content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various stories in the portfolio may be produced/edited by different members; all members recognized. Portfolio should represent diversity throughout the year and must include multimedia stories entered in at least two multimedia categories (#19–22). Include at least three and up to five multimedia stories (as URL links), each under six minutes. Extra $50 per entry for this Premier category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 41 - Environmental Vision Award (Premier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes a photographer's long-term story, project, or essay that explores issues related to the environment, natural history, or science (including human impact, habitat, climate concerns). Not for human medical issues or natural disasters unless proven result of environmental impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a maximum of 40 images. Entries need not have been published. A majority of photos must have been taken during 2013 (historic/establishing images from previous years may be included). Project essay summary: single paragraph (2,000 characters or less) in the story summary field. All photographs must include captions. Previous winners may not be resubmitted. Portions may be entered in Science/Natural History categories and may be part of Photographer of the Year portfolio if photos were taken/published in 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 42 - Community Awareness Award (Premier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes a photographer's extended story or essay that demonstrates understanding of everyday life within a community (broadly defined). Purpose is to encourage attention to small events and celebrate images that reflect work and dreams of humankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a maximum of 40 images. Entries need not have been published. Majority of photos must be taken during 2013 (historic images as support allowed). Project essay summary: single paragraph (2,000 characters or less). All photos must include captions. Winning entries from previous years may not be resubmitted. Portions may be entered in other categories and may be part of a Photographer of the Year portfolio if photos were taken/published in 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 43 - World Understanding Award (Premier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes a photographer's long-term story, project, or essay that focuses on the human condition and portrays sense of justice or insight into difficult problems; topics can include human relations, world conflict, social injustice, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a maximum of 40 images. Entries need not have been published and there are no subject or time restrictions (photos need not have been taken during 2013). Project essay summary: single paragraph (2,000 characters or less). All photos must include captions. Previous World Understanding entries may not be resubmitted for five years. Portions of the essay may not be entered in single or picture story categories, but may be part of a Photographer of the Year portfolio if photos were taken/published in 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 44 - Documentary Project of the Year (Premier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to teams or individuals that best utilize online multimedia components to investigate or explore social, economic, or political issues as a special report, series, or multiple chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project should employ the right mix of still photography, motion photography (video), audio, and graphics to visually communicate the story. Guiding criteria: news value, writing, audio, overall organization, design, clarity of focus, and ease of use. Open to everyone (teams, individuals, agencies, NGOs, media companies). No length criteria. Personal web portfolios, agency catalogs, or business promotions are ineligible. Projects must have been shot, produced, or published during 2013. Provide an active URL to the project's primary web page. Extra $50 for this Premier category, which covers up to three project submissions; three projects count as one "submission" in POY; each project judged separately. Multiple project-entry payment examples explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption and Story Summary Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: All captions and story summaries must meet journalistic standards for accuracy and be ready-for-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions are required for all photographs; story summaries required for picture stories and projects. Judges consider caption effectiveness as part of judging in relevant categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Uniqueness and Reuse Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph may be submitted only once among the single-picture categories; a single photo may appear as part of a picture story in no more than one story; a picture story may be entered only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A published story may be submitted only once. POYi will not separate a portfolio and enter its images in individual categories; upload separate files if you want images considered in other categories. Avoid duplicate entries between agency and photographer that enter same work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia Link and Access Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a single primary URL for each multimedia story; make sure online links are active and accessible through judging dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit password-protected Vimeo links. Provide courtesy logins/passwords if apps are in stores and need credentials for download. Judges will review work as it appears online; ensure URLs are active and current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Page Submission Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit each editing page as a separate PDF file, high quality print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not group pages or embed files together. A doubletruck or spread should be submitted as a single PDF file. A portfolio entry should present less than 40 pages for picture editing portfolios.
